subject.title: Telegram message(action=send) can prematurely release Codex turn in message_tool_only mode

question: Should `message(action=send)` remain terminal by default in `message_tool_only` mode, or should termination require explicit final-delivery intent?
rationale: The runtime cannot reliably infer from a successful send alone whether the assistant intended a progress update or its final source reply, while changing either default affects turn completion and stuck-turn containment.

options.title: Add explicit delivery intent
options.body: Introduce shared internal progress/final result metadata, continue after progress sends, and retain terminal release for explicit final sends.

options.title: Never terminalize message sends
options.body: Treat every successful message send as non-terminal and rely on normal Codex `turn/completed`, accepting possible final-turn liveness regressions.

options.title: Keep terminal-by-default semantics
options.body: Retain the current behavior and document that source-channel progress updates must not use the message tool during an active Codex turn.

recommendation.title: Add explicit delivery intent
recommendation.body: Introduce shared internal progress/final result metadata, continue after progress sends, and retain terminal release for explicit final sends.

likelyOwner.reason: The terminal-release containment behavior and Codex dynamic-tool lifecycle are most directly connected to this person's recent work.
